events.title: Gore by a third
events.text: Al Gore carried Iowa by a third of a percentage point.

events.title: Bush by under a point
events.text: George W. Bush carried Iowa by 0.7 points.

events.title: Harkin re-elected
events.text: Tom Harkin won a fifth Senate term with 62.7 percent, the last Democratic Senate win in Iowa so far.

events.title: Obama by 9.5
events.text: Barack Obama carried Iowa by 9.5 points.

events.title: Thirty-eight counties
events.text: Obama carried Iowa again, by 5.8 points, winning 38 of its 99 counties.

events.title: London bronze
events.text: Josh Turek of Council Bluffs won Paralympic bronze in wheelchair basketball.

events.title: “Make 'em squeal”
events.text: Joni Ernst's primary ad about castrating hogs drew national attention.

events.title: Ernst elected
events.text: Ernst won the open Harkin seat, 52.1 to 43.8 percent over Bruce Braley.

events.title: Trump by 9.4
events.text: Donald Trump carried Iowa by 9.4 points; Clinton won only six counties.

events.title: Thirty-one pivot counties
events.text: Iowa had 31 counties that voted Obama twice, then Trump, the most of any state.

events.title: Rio gold
events.text: Turek won Paralympic gold with the U.S. wheelchair basketball team.

events.title: Hinson elected
events.text: Ashley Hinson, a former KCRG-TV reporter and anchor, won a seat in the Iowa House.

events.title: A Libertarian first
events.text: Thomas Laehn was elected Greene County attorney, the first Libertarian elected to partisan office in Iowa.

events.title: Sand elected auditor
events.text: Democrat Rob Sand was elected state auditor, 51 to 46 percent.

events.title: Hinson to Congress
events.text: Hinson won Iowa's 1st Congressional District.

events.title: Ernst re-elected
events.text: Ernst beat Theresa Greenfield, 51.7 to 45.2 percent, running behind Trump in 89 of 99 counties.

events.title: Trump by 8.2
events.text: Trump carried Iowa again; Biden won six counties.

events.title: Early voting cut
events.text: A new law cut early voting from 29 days to 20.

events.title: Tokyo gold
events.text: Turek won a second Paralympic gold at the Tokyo Games.

events.title: Six votes
events.text: Turek won an Iowa House seat in Council Bluffs by six votes after a recount.

events.title: Grassley's eighth term
events.text: Chuck Grassley was re-elected, 56.0 to 43.8 percent.

events.title: All-Republican delegation
events.text: Republicans won all four U.S. House seats; Sand was the only Democrat to win statewide.

events.title: Caucuses dropped
events.text: The Democratic National Committee left Iowa out of its early 2024 calendar.

events.title: Six-week law
events.text: A ban on most abortions after about six weeks took effect on 29 July.

events.title: A poll misses
events.text: The final Des Moines Register poll showed Harris ahead by three; Trump won by 13.2.

events.title: Scott County flips
events.text: Scott County, home to Davenport, voted Republican for president for the first time since 1984.

events.title: Reynolds steps aside
events.text: Governor Kim Reynolds said she would not seek re-election.

events.title: Parkersburg town hall
events.text: Answering a question on Medicaid cuts, Ernst said: “Well, we all are going to die.”

events.title: Hinson votes yes
events.text: Hinson voted for the 2025 tax-and-spending law that reduced Medicaid spending.

events.title: Turek enters
events.text: On 12 August Turek announced a run for the Senate.

events.title: Ernst retires
events.text: On 2 September Ernst said she would not run again; Hinson entered the race hours later.

events.title: Trump endorses Hinson
events.text: On 5 September President Trump endorsed Hinson.

events.title: Laehn runs
events.text: On 7 October Laehn announced a Libertarian campaign for the Senate.

events.title: Ernst backs Hinson
events.text: In January Ernst endorsed Hinson at a Dallas County event.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 2 June Turek beat Zach Wahls, 62.7 to 37.3 percent; Hinson beat Jim Carlin, 74.2 to 25.8.

events.title: A toss-up
events.text: On 20 August the Cook Political Report moved the race to toss-up.

events.title: First debate
events.text: On 7 October Hinson and Turek debated on Iowa PBS in Johnston.

events.title: Early voting opens
events.text: Iowa's twenty-day early-voting period began on 14 October.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Iowans choose between Hinson, Turek and Laehn.

chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; FEC certified results). It is a simplification: Iowa elects its senator in its own race, and Iowans have split their tickets (in 2020 Senator Ernst ran about 1.6 points behind President Trump's margin), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Iowa, so outer states are cut at the edge.
